answer: Vertex-Weighted Thread Binding: each new identity must reference an existing identity as its parent, and that edge's weight grows with every downstream registration. Splitting into many identities forces each to pay an increasing marginal registration cost tied to its parent's cumulative branching, so wide fan-out becomes expensive fast. The velvet zone is a small grace allowance for genuinely new entrants; beyond it, per-identity cost scales superlinearly, making a sybil cluster cost far more than honest parallel registration.
